result.summary: No context condition brings the a5 -> C1 edge below ~11 bits. Symbolically (symext.py, extending elim/a10/symeng.py with arbitrary-constant offsets e_r = a_{r-4} + t and rotational ties), with a0..a3 known a5 reaches C1 through W10 alone, inside exactly four atoms: -Sigma0(a5) (top level, from -e6), +Sigma1(a5 + c9) (from e9), -Maj(a5,a4,a3), +Ch(a5+c9,e8,e7). Neither one-input map has a context partner, no second occurrence exists anywhere in C1 to cancel against, and the context can only kill the Maj/Ch atoms and choose c9. Numerically, over 22,176 enumerated configurations (3,872 legal: a6/a7 equalities, complements, 11 rotations; e8 at 8 constants; e9 - a5 at 10 constants via a9 = c9 + T2(a8,a7,a6)), plus 360 e10/e11 variants and a 3,058-value sweep of c9, a5 -> C1 ranges 10.87-12.76 bits (mean 11.98); control a4 -> C0 is 11.6-13.2 (13.1 in the best condition, 12.3 random context, matching the paper). Nothing below 4 bits. Attribution: freezing e9 (illegal diagnostic) leaves the Sigma0(a5) atom alone at 6.4 bits; Sigma1(e9) lifts it to ~12; in closed form Sigma1(x) - Sigma0(x) costs 10.35 bits per flip where the XOR would be 6, i.e. the modular subtraction between two rotation maps is the barrier. Tying a4 = phi(a5) or a9 = f(a5) is illegal (a5 is absorbed by C3, which needs a1,a2,a3 through W3 and s0(W4), so a5 is last and every context word must be known at C0 time); evaluated anyway in the illegal frame these ties make C0 15.7-16.1 and C1 12.2-16.3. Side-finding: a6 = ~a4, a7 = a6, e8 = -1, e10 = -1, e11 = 0 makes a5 exactly absent from C0 and C2 and exactly linear in C3, so the a5 problem is precisely the single C1 edge (11.3 bits there). The 20-round barrier stands; the offset-law prediction is confirmed with a wider menu.

result.summary: The a5 -> C1 edge does not crack under an extended condition menu, and its residual has no exploitable structure. Extended menu (a5 the unknown, never referenced; legality checked numerically as invariance of the realised context under changes of a5): a6 vs a4 in {free, =, ~, 31 rotations, 31 rotations of the complement, 17 xor-constants, 17 add-constants}; a7 vs a6 in {free, =, ~}; e8 = any of 17 constants (incl. 0, -1, 2^31, 2^31-1, 0x5555.., 0xAAAA.., byte/half masks, 1, random); e9 = a5 + any of 17 offsets (the offset c9 is a knob outside the standard menu, set through a9); then on top of the best bases e10, e11 = 17 constants each (sat_r and sat_h), a7 rotational/xor/add ties, a4 tied to digest words. 98,908 configurations enumerated, 38,150 legal, each measured with 200 random states x all 32 single-bit flips of a5 (context re-realised after the flip), reporting the exact C1 table index (T1 - W2) and the C0 index. Result: a5 -> C1 = 10.86 min / 11.90 mean / 12.77 max bits per flipped bit over the class; nothing below 10.85, so nothing below the 4-bit WEAK threshold or the 2-bit crack threshold. The only knob that moves the edge at all is the e9 offset: e9 = a5 + 0 (or + 2^31) removes the carry chain inside Sigma1(a5 + c9) and lowers the weight from ~12.1 to ~10.9 bits; rotational, xor and additive ties between a4 and a6 do nothing (11.05-12.77), e8 constants other than {0,-1} do nothing (10.90-12.68), e10/e11 do not reach W10 at all (C1 invariant, 11.15-12.46 across 2,510 configs). Meanwhile a5 -> C0 ranges 0.00 (absent, with a6 = ~a4, a7 = a6, e8 = -1) to 11.10, C2 0.92-2.49, C3 0.91-1.68 (exactly linear with e11 = 0); control a4 -> C0 = 12.31 bits (random context; 12.4 with a7 = a6, e9 = -1), matching the paper's 12.2. Structure: the a5-dependence of the C1 index is exactly f(a5) = const - Sigma0(a5) - Maj(a5,a4,a3) + Sigma1(a5 + c9) + Ch(a5 + c9, e8, e7(a5)) (verified bit-exact on 16,384 states and on 2^20-sample assertions per scanned state, in every configuration where Maj(a7,a6,a5) is collapsed). Its 32x32 sensitivity matrix is a rotation-structured band (Sigma0 rows at offsets 2/13/22, Sigma1 at 6/11/25) smeared by carries: mean 0.343 (best config) / 0.379 (best standard config), only 108/1024 resp. 28/1024 cells deterministic, NO output bit is GF(2)-affine in a5, no input bit acts deterministically, GF(2) rank of the majority Jacobian 31 (the known all-ones kernel of Sigma0 xor Sigma1), whole-word GF(2)-linearity probability 0, and the additive difference f(a5 ^ e_i) - f(a5) takes 96-192 (best) or up to 7,130 (standard) distinct values per input bit where a borrow-free/bitwise dependence would allow at most 2. So the C1 residual under a provisional freeze of a5 is not bitwise on any subset of bits. Exhaustive 2^32 residual scans rho(a5) = idx(a5) - idx(a5_prov) at fixed state: #{rho = 0} = 1, 2, 2, 2 (best config, four a5_prov incl. 0 and -1), 3, 2 (best standard config), 3 (a6 = a4 ^ 2^31 variant); #{rho = 0 mod 2^8} = 16,777,216 / 16,777,213 / 16,777,196 (i.e. exactly 2^-8), mod 2^16 = 65,279-66,389 (2^-16), mod 2^24 = 241-270 (2^-24); popcount(rho) <= 4 counts 41,046-41,616 vs 41,449 uniform. Full histograms of the index over all 2^32 a5: 0.63233 x 2^32 and 0.63213 x 2^32 distinct values, max multiplicity 12 and 11, sum n_v^2 = 1.9989 x 2^32 and 1.9999 x 2^32, hence E_{a5_prov} P(rho = 0) = 1.999 x 2^-32 and 2.000 x 2^-32: the C1 index as a function of a5 is statistically a random map of 2^32 points. No condition raises P(residual = 0) above 2^-32 by more than the generic random-function factor 2 (threshold was 4), and none produces a (3/4)^32-type bitwise condition. The prediction of the offset law holds: the blocking atom Sigma0(a5) is additive in W10 with no context partner, and the only other one-input term Sigma1(a5 + c9) cannot cancel it for any constant c9.

result.summary: The a5 -> C1 edge stays heavy under every context assignment tested, in the reduced-width model and at full width. Method: a w-bit SHA-256 analogue (wmodel.py; rotation amounts scaled as in paper_r20_barrier.tex; at w=32 it reproduces SHA-256 and submask_family.py word for word and the prior numbers exactly: a5 with a7=a6,e8=-1 gives C0 0.94 / C1 12.04 / C2 1.45 / C3 1.42; a4->C0 control 12.33). Key structural fact, verified numerically at w=5,6,8,12,32 (66,000/66,000 checks at w=32): when a8..a11 are free the C1 lookup target is T1 = c'(state) - G(a5) with G = S0(a5) + Maj(a5,a4,a3) - S1(a5+c9) - Ch(a5+c9, c8-Maj(a7,a6,a5), c7-Maj(a6,a5,a4)), c9 = a9-S0(a8)-Maj(a8,a7,a6), c8 = a4+a8-S0(a7), c7 = a3+a7-S0(a6); (a8,a9)<->(c8,c9) is bijective, so every tie among a4,a6,a7 and every value of a8..a11 is a point of the (a4,a6,a7,c8,c9) space and can be enumerated. Results (bits per flipped bit of a5 into the C1 target; heavy control a4->C0 = 2.56/2.85/3.30/6.42/12.33 at w=5/6/8/12/32; a purely linear entry = 1.6-1.9; Maj/Ch-only = 0.8-1.0): w=5 LITERALLY EXHAUSTIVE over all 2^25 = 33,554,432 context assignments with all 32 values of a3: min 2.133, none below 2.0 (0/33.5M), full round function confirms 2.14-2.17. w=8: all 2^24 kernel constants (c9,X,Y): min 2.316, none below 2.0; all 2^24 (v,c8,c9) of the family a4=a6=a7=v: min 2.518, none below 2.5; all 2^24 (a4^a6 mask, c8, c9) of the family a7=a6: min 2.677; 2,097,152 random general contexts: min 2.640, none below 2.5; structural sweep of 136,185 legal configurations (all 16 free/saturation patterns of a8..a11 incl. e_i via a_i, e_{i+4} via a_i, e_{i+1} via Sigma0-inversion, constants 0/-1/random, 61 tie families incl. all rotations, complements, additive/xor ties, digest ties, constants): min 3.028; all 256 constants for a saturated e9 (117,504 configs): min 3.343 and C0 heavy (>= 3.84). w=6: 16,777,216 of 2^30: min 2.313, none below 2.0. w=12: 262,144 random contexts: min 6.13 (mean 6.40, sd 0.06), 262,144 kernel samples: min 5.98; none below 3. w=32 (reduction, 64 states x 32 flips): 262,144 random contexts min 11.67 mean 12.31; structured families 65,536 each: a4=a6=a7 11.40, a7=a6/a4=~a6/e8=-1 11.55, |c9|<=8 11.09, both 10.99 (mean 11.48); 0 of 524,288 full-width contexts below 4 bits. The minima have a consistent shape (c9 in {+-2,+-4}, i.e. e9 = a5 + tiny constant so S1(a5+c9) ~ S1(a5), and Ch passing few bits of e9) that removes at most 10-25% of the heavy weight and does not grow with width (min/control 0.83, 0.81, 0.76, 0.95, 0.89 at w=5,6,8,12,32); predicted w=32 minimum ~11 bits, measured 11.0-11.4. Injectivity: a5 -> C1target is random-function-like at every width (image (1-1/e)2^w, mean fibre 1.6-2.5, max fibre <= 11 at w<=12, smallest image 106/256 in 2^24 contexts), every bit of a5 moves the target in 100% of states at w=32 (>= 84% at w<=8), so there is no structured non-injectivity and the number of a5 consistent with a fixed C1 target is ~1-2. Side findings: a5 can be made exactly ABSENT from C0 (a7=a6, a6=~a4, e8=-1: Maj(~a4,a5,a4)=a5 cancels -a5 from e5; C0 = 0.000 at w=8,12,32) while C2 and C3 stay Maj-mild (0.98), and exactly absent from C2 (e10=0 with a4=a6=a7) or from C3 (e11=-1); in all such contexts C1 stays at 11.3-12.2 bits at full width. No WEAK edge (< 4 bits) was found anywhere.
result.best_condition: a7 = a6 = v, a4 = ~v, e8 = -1 (solved through a8, i.e. c8 = a4+a8-Sigma0(a7) = v-1), and a9 = Sigma0(a8) + Maj(a8,a7,a6) so that c9 = 0 (e9 = a5 exactly); a10, a11 free. Full width, all a0..a3 and digest words random: a5 -> C0 = 0.00 exactly, C1 = 11.0-11.4 bits (kernel Sigma0(a5) - Sigma1(a5) - Ch(a5, X, Y) + Maj terms), C2 = 0.98, C3 = 0.98 (1.96 = exactly linear with e11 = 0). result.verdict: EDGE STAYS HEAVY. No widened condition class weakened the a5 -> C1 edge. Across five independent explorers (constants, rotational/linear ties, Sigma-cancellation, extended menu with residual structure, reduced-width exhaustion), roughly 1.59 million legal context conditions at full width plus ~105 million exhaustive or random value assignments at reduced widths, the lowest legal weight is 10.86 bits per flipped bit of a5 (the standard-menu floor is 12.1). Zero conditions fall below 4 bits (WEAK), zero below 10.85, so nothing approaches the 2-bit crack threshold. The only sub-4-bit numbers seen anywhere (7.2-8.1 bits) come from conditions that make a9 depend on a5 itself, which is illegal in the absorption frame and in any case sends a5 -> C0/C2/C3 to 15+ bits. The 20-round barrier stands; the offset-law prediction of FINDINGS.md is confirmed on a much wider menu.
result.plain_english: You asked whether any condition on the context words could quietly defuse the one edge that stops a5 from being absorbed at 20 rounds: the Sigma0(a5) sitting inside e6 in W10, which is how a5 reaches the C1 lookup. Five separate searches, using different code paths, attacked it from different directions: every constant you can pin (e8, e9's offset, e10, e11, a6, a7, a4, all the way to 100,000 random values of each and 160,000 random pairs); every rotation, XOR, additive, Sigma0/Sigma1 and GF(2)-linear tie between context words (145,645 conditions); an explicit symbolic hunt for a second occurrence of Sigma0(a5) or Sigma1 that could cancel it; an extended-menu sweep with a full 2^32 scan of the residual's structure; and a reduced-width model that at 5 bits was literally exhaustive over all 2^25 contexts. All of them find the same thing. Once a0..a3 and the context are fixed, the C1 target depends on a5 exactly through four atoms, -Sigma0(a5) - Maj(a5,a4,a3) + Sigma1(a5+c9) + Ch(a5+c9, e8, e7), and the context has only two levers: it can flatten the Maj/Ch terms (worth about 1-2 bits) and it can choose the constant c9 = a9 - T2(a8,a7,a6). The modular difference Sigma1(a5+c9) - Sigma0(a5) never drops below 10.3 bits for any c9 (201,058 values scanned, including every sparse one), and nothing else in the context reaches W10 at all: e10, e11, a10, a11 and the digest words provably leave the a5-difference in T1 bit-identical. So the best you can do is c9 in {0, 2^31} with a7 = a6 = a4 (or ~a4) and e8 = -1, which lands at 10.9-11.0 bits, and the residual is statistically a random 32-bit map: no output bit is affine in a5, the additive difference takes hundreds to thousands of distinct values per flipped bit, and P(residual = 0) is 2 x 2^-32, exactly the random-function value. The consolation finding, reproduced by four of the five explorers, is that a5 can be made exactly absent from C0 (a6 = ~a4, a7 = a6, e8 = -1) and from C2, and exactly linear in C3, so the entire 20-round obstruction really is this single C1 edge and nothing else. That is a clean statement for the barrier note, but it is a statement of where the wall is, not a hole in it. Attacking it further would need something that is not a context condition: a different unknown ordering, or a way to control a9 that does not leak a5 into W17 and sigma1(W15).
result.for_the_record: The a5 -> C1 edge at R=20 (a5 entering the C1 lookup target through -Sigma0(a5) in e6 = a2 + a6 - Sigma0(a5) - Maj(a5,a4,a3) inside W10) was tested against widened context-condition classes in five independent studies, all CPU-only, each measuring bits changed in the C1 target per single-bit flip of a5 over 200 random states (a0..a3, digest words random; context re-realised after the flip; legality = realised context invariant under change of a5), with the a4 -> C0 edge as heavy control (12.3-13.1 bits, paper: 12.2). (1) Constants: 1,145,175 conditions (1,144,419 legal) over e8, c9 = e9 - a5 (via a9), e10, e11, a6, a7, a4 in {0, -1, 23 structured, 60 single-bit masks/complements, ROTR-invariant patterns, up to 100,000 random values each; 26^4 structured 4-tuples; 160,000 e8 x c9 pairs; 270,000 random pairs with a6, a4}: a5 -> C1 min 10.92 / mean 11.98 / max 12.68 bits. (2) Rotational and linear ties: 145,645 conditions (46,989 strict) covering a7 = ROTR^n(a6), a6 = ROTR^n(a4), a7 = ROTR^n(a4) for all n, rotational ties for every ordered pair among a4, a6..a11, XOR/additive/Sigma0/Sigma1/Maj ties, all 496 weight-2 and 600 sampled weight-3 GF(2)-linear ties per pair, all 1,024 double rotations, each crossed with e8..e11 in {free, 0, -1}: strict min 11.86 / mean 12.31 / max 12.51; non-strict (a9 carrying a5) min 8.13 with a5 -> C0 15.8, C2 16.0, C3 12.4. (3) Sigma-cancellation audit: symbolic engine shows a5 reaches C1 through W10 alone in exactly four atoms (-Sigma0(a5), +Sigma1(a5+c9), -Maj(a5,a4,a3), +Ch(a5+c9,e8,e7)) with no second occurrence anywhere in C1; 22,176 configurations (3,872 legal) + 360 e10/e11 variants + 3,058-value c9 sweep: min 10.87 / mean 11.98 / max 12.76; closed form Sigma1(x) - Sigma0(x) costs 10.35 bits/flip vs 6 for the XOR. (4) Extended menu and residual structure: 98,908 configurations (38,150 legal; a6 vs a4 in 31 rotations, 31 complement-rotations, 17 XOR and 17 additive constants; e8 and the e9 offset at 17 constants each; e10/e11 at 17 constants each): min 10.855 / mean 11.90 / max 12.77; e10, e11, a10, a11 and digest words leave the a5-difference of T1 bit-identical; 32 x 32 sensitivity matrix mean 0.343, no GF(2)-affine output bit, majority-Jacobian rank 31, 96-7,130 distinct additive differences per input bit; exhaustive 2^32 residual scans give #{rho = 0} in {1,2,3}, index histogram 0.6323 x 2^32 distinct values, sum n_v^2 = 1.999 x 2^32, i.e. E P(rho = 0) = 2.0 x 2^-32 (random-map value; threshold was 4 x 2^-32). (5) Reduced-width model (w-bit SHA-256 analogue, rotations scaled as in paper_r20_barrier.tex, w = 32 reproduces SHA-256 exactly): reduction T1 = c' - G(a5) verified exactly at w = 5, 6, 8, 12, 32 with (a8, a9) <-> (c8, c9) bijective; w = 5 literally exhaustive over all 2^25 contexts x 32 values of a3: min 2.133 vs control 2.56, 0 of 33.5M below 2.0; w = 6: 16.8M contexts, min 2.313; w = 8: three exhaustive 2^24 families + 2.1M random + 136,185 structural + 117,504 e9-constant configurations, min 2.316 vs control 3.30; w = 12: 524,288 contexts, min 5.98 vs control 6.42; w = 32: 524,288 contexts, min 10.99 vs control 12.33; min/control ratio 0.76-0.95 at every width, not decreasing. Combined: ~1.59 million legal full-width conditions and ~105 million reduced-width value assignments; global legal minimum 10.855 bits (a6 = a4 ^ 2^31 or a6 = a4, a7 = a6, e8 = -1 via a8, e9 = a5 exactly via a9 = T2(a8,a7,a6); a10, a11 free), the same family (c9 in {0, 2^31}, a7 = a6 = a4 or ~a4, e8 = -1) found by all five studies at 10.86-10.99; 0 conditions below 4 bits (WEAK), 0 below 10.85; refuters (fresh seeds, 1,000 states, independent scalar implementations) agree within 0.37 bits. Kernel Sigma1(a5 + c9) - Sigma0(a5) >= 10.27 bits for every c9 in a 201,058-value scan including all c9 with <= 2 set or <= 2 clear bits; Maj + Ch residual 0.9-1.9 bits is the entire lever available to the context. Side result: a5 is exactly absent from C0 (a6 = ~a4, a7 = a6, e8 = -1; 0.000 bits at w = 8, 12, 32) and from C2, and exactly linear in C3 with e11 = 0, so the 20-round obstruction is precisely the single a5 -> C1 edge. No refutations were filed.
